title: Humanized but Still True? Auditing Facts and Detection in AI-Text Humanizers
author: Ziyuan Wang, Genliang Zhu, Xiaobo Chen

summary: AI "humanizers" rewrite machine-generated text so that detectors classify it as human-written. Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive.
takeaways: Unit retention and detector evasion were not clearly related across tools (Spearman rho = -0.46, 95% CI -0.65 to 0.08), and the open model's four released files (two of them quantization-aware low-bit files) did not show the pre-registered monotone trade-off.
Public leaderboards score evasion and embedding similarity, but not whether checkable details survive.
In the October 2026 cycle of a public humanizer leaderboard, all 11 commercial tools changed or dropped at least one of these units in 35-65% of the documents that contained one.
